memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Lead on Relative Strength; AAPL, XOM, and UNH in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of today. MSFT and NVDA are the standout leaders: MSFT sits just 3.7% off its 52-week high with 4-week relative strength vs SPY of +9.7% and +13.1% for NVDA, both trading well above their 50- and 200-day means. On the other side, UNH is in freefall—down 52.7% from its high, RSI at 27.1, and 34.4% below its 50-day mean with no sign of stabilization beyond a feeble +1.3% bounce this week. AAPL and XOM are also breaking down, both below their 50- and 200-day averages with RSIs near 38 and persistent negative relative strength. I would ride the momentum leaders and avoid the broken charts until price proves otherwise.

views.note: Trading +11.6% above 50d mean, only 3.7% off highs, RSI 66.8 strong but not overbought; would reassess on a close below 420 (roughly the 50d mean).
4-week return +18.3% with +13.1% relative strength vs SPY, price +14.4% above 50d mean; extended but trend is clearly up—would cut on a close below 115.
Down 24.6% from 52w high, 13.6% below 200d mean, RSI 38.7, and 4w relative strength vs SPY is -11.9%; no reason to step in until price reclaims 206 (approx 50d mean).
RSI 27.1, 52.7% drawdown from high, 44% below 200d mean with 7.1% daily ATR—this is a falling knife with no technical base; would reconsider only above 350.
Below both moving averages, RSI 38.4, 4w relative strength vs SPY -10.3%; persistent downtrend—need a close above 109 to reconsider.
Only 6.9% off highs, above both moving averages with positive relative strength, RSI 59.8 healthy; would exit below 245.
Strong 4w bounce (+12.1%) but still 4% below 200d mean and 17.6% off highs—momentum improving but not yet confirmed; watching for a close above 360.
Sitting right at its 200d mean with middling RSI of 54.9 and flat 12w relative strength; no edge either way until it clears 215 or breaks 190.

Low volatility (ATR 1.4%), hugging its 50d mean, RSI 56.8—defensive and dull, no directional signal here.

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Show Durable Earnings Power; CAT and XOM Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see the clearest fundamental quality in GOOGL and MSFT this quarter. GOOGL posted 12% YoY revenue growth to $90.2B with a stunning 38.3% net margin and net income up 46% YoY on only $14.8B of total debt—this is the best margin-to-leverage profile in the universe. MSFT delivered 13.3% revenue growth to $70.1B with a 36.9% net margin and 17.7% net income growth, all on manageable $42.9B debt. On the other end, CAT's revenue fell 9.8% YoY to $14.3B with net income collapsing 29.8%, signaling real cyclical earnings compression that I refuse to pay for at current levels. XOM is similarly uninspiring: flat revenue (+0.1%) and a 6.2% decline in net income to $7.7B with a thin 9.3% margin—I'd need to see commodity prices stabilize and margins recover before getting constructive.

views.note: 38.3% net margin, 46% YoY net income growth, and minimal leverage ($14.8B debt) represent best-in-class durable earnings power.
13.3% revenue growth with 36.9% net margin and 17.7% net income growth on moderate $42.9B debt is a high-quality compounder profile.
77.9% YoY revenue growth and 56.2% net margin are extraordinary, though the last filing is from January and I need the upcoming quarter to confirm sustainability.
64.2% YoY net income growth and margin expansion to 11.0% show operating leverage kicking in, though $58.8B debt and still-thin margins warrant monitoring.
Revenue growth of only 5.1% and net income growth of 4.8% on $92.2B of total debt is pedestrian for the valuation; I'd need accelerating top-line to get constructive.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% net income growth, but bank-specific leverage ($407B debt) and macro sensitivity keep me at neutral.
Revenue declined 2.1% YoY to $19.8B with net income barely growing 0.4%—stable but no earnings momentum to justify a long.
9.8% revenue growth to $109.6B is decent but 5.7% net margin and $81.3B debt with unavailable YoY net income comparison leave too many open questions.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY is textbook cyclical earnings compression; margin would need to stabilize above 16% to reconsider.
Flat revenue and a 6.2% decline in net income to a 9.3% margin on $32.8B debt signals commodity headwinds with no near-term catalyst for margin recovery.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Cooling CPI and Rising Unemployment — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I read the current macro regime as a prolonged pause with an easing bias: the fed funds upper bound has been flat at 4.50% for three months, yet is down 100 bp year-over-year, while CPI is running at just 2.3% y/y — close enough to target that the next move is more likely a cut than a hike. Unemployment at 4.2% has crept up 30 bp over the past year, signaling a softening labor market that should keep the Fed from tightening further. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+97 bp y/y to +0.54 pp), which historically supports bank net interest margins but also reflects the market pricing in eventual easing. I have moderate conviction in duration-sensitive mega-cap growth names that benefit from a lower-rate trajectory, and I am cautious on pure cyclicals like CAT given the labor-market softening. A hot May CPI print (above 0.4% m/m) or a surprise rate hike would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a pause-to-easing regime with 2.3% CPI and a steepening curve.
Lower forward rate path supports valuations for long-duration equities; benign inflation backdrop is constructive.
High-multiple growth name stands to gain most from rate cuts, though 10y at 4.51% keeps a lid on near-term multiple expansion.
Steepening curve (+54 bp 10y-2y) aids NIM, but rising unemployment at 4.2% raises credit-loss concerns — effects roughly offset.
Cyclical exposure is unattractive with unemployment trending higher (+0.3 pp y/y) and no signs of re-acceleration.
Staples offer defensive ballast but limited upside in a regime where growth equities are favored by falling rate expectations.
Energy is macro-neutral here; softening demand signals from labor market offset any inflation hedge appeal.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: MSFT and JPM Momentum vs. UNH Distress and AAPL/PG Drag
memos.body: I see the sharpest sentiment divergence across the universe in weeks. MSFT's +7.6% post-earnings pop on 4/30 is the strongest positive price reaction in this group and signals a genuine narrative upgrade around cloud/AI execution; JPM's +4.0% earnings-day move and steady stream of Reg FD filings through 5/22 suggest sustained institutional engagement. On the negative side, UNH's -22.4% earnings-day crash on 4/17 followed by three consecutive C-suite departure filings (4/29, 5/14, 5/21) points to an ongoing governance crisis where negative tone is likely still intensifying rather than stabilizing. AAPL (-3.7% post-earnings) and PG (-3.7% post-earnings) both disappointed, but their subsequent filing activity has been routine, suggesting the negative sentiment shock may be largely absorbed. I have highest conviction on MSFT's positive momentum and UNH's continued negative spiral, and lower conviction elsewhere where price reactions were muted.

views.note: The +7.6% earnings-day reaction is the strongest in the universe and suggests a durable positive narrative shift around AI/cloud that likely has further room to run in media tone.
A +4.0% earnings pop plus five 8-K filings through 5/22 indicate sustained positive institutional attention and constructive sentiment flow.
The -22.4% earnings crash followed by three separate officer departure filings in four weeks signals an accelerating negative narrative that is unlikely to have been fully priced.
The -3.7% post-earnings dip was notable but subsequent filings are routine; negative sentiment shock appears largely digested with no clear directional catalyst.
A -3.7% earnings-day drop mirrors AAPL's pattern; the dividend declaration and routine 8-K suggest stable but uninspiring tone with limited further downside from sentiment alone.
A +1.7% earnings pop and four 8-K filings in three weeks suggest moderately positive and broadening media attention, though the move is less decisive than MSFT's.
Essentially flat (-0.1%) post-earnings reaction signals the market already priced in the narrative; no strong sentiment tilt either way.
A muted +0.6% earnings reaction and routine officer-change filings leave sentiment directionless; I see no clear tone inflection.
A +0.4% post-earnings move is noise; filing activity is routine and I detect no meaningful sentiment shift.
Only one non-earnings 8-K on file with no price reaction data; insufficient sentiment signal to take a directional view ahead of its upcoming report.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Still Elevated on 3-Month Basis Despite Recent Easing; Export-Control Risk Keeps NVDA in Focus
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 283.69 has fallen 35% over the past month but remains nearly 40% above its level three months ago, signaling that while the acute tariff/sanctions shock may be fading, the structural policy overhang has not cleared. VIX at 20.28 tells a similar story: down sharply month-over-month yet still elevated versus early-year levels. WTI crude at $62.55 is off 11.6% over three months, which eases energy-cost pressure for importers but signals demand-side weakness that could reflect trade-friction drag on global activity. High-yield OAS widened 54 bp over three months to 3.32%, consistent with credit markets still pricing residual geopolitical risk. I have highest conviction on NVDA's vulnerability to further China export controls (its April 8-K flagged an 'Other Events' disclosure around the time of tightened AI-chip restrictions) and on CAT's exposure to tariff-driven capex uncertainty, while JPM and PG look relatively insulated from direct supply-chain or export-control risk.

views.note: NVDA's April 8-K coincided with tightened AI-chip export controls to China; any further restriction escalation would hit its data-center revenue directly, and I would need a formal licensing safe-harbor to turn constructive.
Two 8-Ks in a month and elevated policy uncertainty suggest tariff-driven capex hesitation among CAT's industrial customers; a credible trade deal or tariff rollback would change my view.

AAPL's China manufacturing concentration remains a structural risk, but the recent drop in policy uncertainty and its May 8-K suggest management is actively managing the narrative; I lack detail to take a directional view.
WTI at $62.55 and falling 3-month trend reflect demand-side softness possibly tied to trade friction; XOM is somewhat insulated by domestic production but lower crude caps upside.

JPM faces limited direct export-control or tariff exposure; a steeper yield curve (10y-2y spread +31 bp over 3 months) supports NIM, and multiple Reg-FD filings suggest proactive investor communication.
PG's defensive profile and domestic revenue skew make it a relative safe haven amid elevated policy uncertainty; its multiple 8-Ks suggest routine disclosure rather than geopolitical stress.

plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 420 (roughly the 50-day mean) would invalidate the momentum thesis and trigger an exit.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst's top pick (0.90) with 38.3% net margin and 46% YoY net income growth on minimal leverage. Sentiment moderately positive (+1.7% earnings pop). Technicals are neutral/range-bound, so sized slightly below MSFT, but the valuation-to-quality ratio is compelling.
